points.label: Saul’s action
points.left: Saul approves and ravages the assembly. Acts 8:1–3 belongs to Saul, witness and opponent.
points.right: Saul proclaims in Damascus and escapes. Acts 9:19–25 belongs to Encounter and first witness.

points.label: Message and opposition
points.left: Saul approves and ravages the assembly. Saul was consenting to his death. A great persecution arose against the assembly which was in Jerusalem in that day. They were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except for the apostles. But Saul ravaged the assembly, entering into every house and dragged both men and women off to prison.
points.right: Saul proclaims in Damascus and escapes. He took food and was strengthened. Saul stayed several days with the disciples who were at Damascus. but his disciples took him by night and let him down through the wall, lowering him in a basket.

payload.posture: Inspect what each source actually says before relating their chronology, argument, or remembered scene.

payload.tension: Approving death and proclaiming life places two independently valuable sources together while preserving their distinct audience, form, sequence, and stated purpose.
